title: Ordinary strictly perfect evaluation is degreewise invertible
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U$ an open, and $P,F$ complexes of sheaves of $\mathcal O_U$-modules, with $P$ strictly perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Put $S=\mathcal O_U[0]$ and $D=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,S)$ [def-pur-hom-complex]. Let $f:\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes D)\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,F)$ be a chain map [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Require that on the tensor summand $F^p\otimes D^q$ in degree $n=p+q$, its projection to $\mathcal Hom(P^r,F^{r+n})$ is zero if $r+q\ne0$; if $r+q=0$, it is the currying of evaluation of $D^q$ on $P^r$, followed by the unit action on $F^p$ [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. Then every $f^n$ is an isomorphism. No boundedness is required of $F$ and $U$ need not be affine.

proof.text: The product projections of Hom(P,S) identify its degree-q term with Hom(P^(-q),O). The other target terms of S are zero, so their Hom objects are zero.

Bounded support of P gives finitely many potentially nonzero dual terms and Hom factors. Identify each total degree with the finite sum indexed by p+q=n; the component predicate makes f block diagonal with the ordinary module evaluation comparisons.

For a finite free module E, identify Hom(E,B) and B tensor Hom(E,O) with finitely many copies of B. Evaluation on basis sections identifies the comparison with the identity. Naturality of the tensor-Hom bijection transports these identifications to any retract of E, and restricts the inverse to the retract.
The finite sum of these isomorphisms is invertible. The same formulas apply to empty U, zero P, and rank-zero modules.
